thread:
marta: Quick thought — when an upstream scales down mid-stream we currently either abort the client or restart the whole generation. Both are bad (latency + token waste). What do folks think about a "soft rehandshake" where the runtime emits tiny checkpoints and the gateway attempts a midstream rehandshake to continue from the last checkpoint?

alex: I like trying to avoid full restarts. Main concerns: (1) side effects/non-idempotent streams, (2) leaking context/PII, (3) complexity of replay semantics. We should gate resumability strictly.

sam: Implementation sketch: runtime emits periodic checkpoint events (opaque base64 blobs) every N tokens. Gateway stores only an encrypted handle and TTL. On failover we spin up or warm a compatible upstream and present the checkpoint to resume. Example wire hints:

```
X-RW-Resume-ID: rsm_20260323_01
Trailer: Resume-Accepted: true|false
X-RW-Checkpoint: base64(eyJvZmYiOjUwLCJjb250ZXh0IjoiLi4uIn0=)
```

marta: Ops constraints: TTL short (30s-2m), per-tenant storage cap, encrypted with KMS, and strict ACLs so handles don’t escape tenant boundary. Also require trace id propagation so resumed requests map to the same trace and billing.

ops-bot: FYI staging deploy with prototype turned on: edge.resume_rehandshake flag=false by default. Deploy #2026.03.23-rc3.

leo: Security note: checkpoints may contain model state or user PII. We need an upstream annotation like `resume:allowed` from runtime or an explicit opt-in header from customers. Otherwise gateway MUST drop checkpoint metadata. Also require an explicit data-retention policy in RFC.

alex: UX decision: expose resume id to clients via response header so clients can retry with hint, or keep it internal only. Trailers are ideal logically but client libs / browsers often don't support trailers reliably. Suggest we expose header + optional trailer.

sam: Phased rollout plan:
- Phase 0: no resume.
- Phase 1: runtime emits ephemeral checkpoints; gateway keeps in-memory handle TTL=30s; resume only within same availability zone; gated by feature flag.
- Phase 2: encrypted persistent handles (short-lived DB/kv) for cross-AZ resume and longer windows; opt-in per-route.
- Phase 3: surface metrics and dashboards (resume.attempts, resume.successes, resume.failure_reasons, tokens_saved, avg_resume_latency).

marta: RFC checklist items: authoritative definition of "checkpoint-safe", per-tenant storage limits, per-route opt-in/opt-out, interaction with retry budgets (should consumption count against retry budget?), telemetry markers for billing and SLOs, and a clear fallback behavior (send partial + X-RW-Partial: true). Also add an API header `X-RW-Resume-Opt-Out: true` for customers who don't want any resume artifacts.

alex: Also important: resumed responses must be annotated in logs/metrics so they don't hide upstream instability. We should tag them and possibly exempt them from normal SLO calculations or at least make them visible.

sam: Small nit: add `Resume-Accepted` trailer so clients know whether the gateway used the resume hint or not. That helps client-side heuristics.

leo: I'll kick off a security review once the RFC is drafted. Also require a threat model section covering malicious resume IDs, replay attacks, and tenant isolation.

marta: Sounds good. I'll draft the RFC this afternoon: interface, security checklist, telemetry hooks, and a minimal prototype plan. Tagging @eng-runtime, @eng-security, @product. If no objections, I'll open the PR and link to staging deploy and a little dashboard. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup: add a canary experiment to measure tokens saved vs resume cost before enabling more broadly.

marta: Good call. I'll include an experiment plan and success criteria (e.g., >30% token savings for resumed flows, <0.5% incorrect resume rate). Will ping here when RFC PR is up.
